subject.title: Manage Claw cron jobs through the gateway

question: Should experimental Claw cron ownership require `agents delete` to become the canonical scheduler-cleanup path in this stack, or should Claw cron jobs be explicitly modeled as surviving ordinary agent deletion?
rationale: The branch deliberately chooses the latter while the prior review requires the former; this determines the durable ownership contract and cannot be resolved safely by a mechanical patch without maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt canonical agent cleanup
options.body: Update the shared agent-deletion path to remove and reconcile agent-owned cron jobs, with Claw removal layering only Claw-specific provenance cleanup around it.

options.title: Define surviving schedules
options.body: Keep ordinary deletion unchanged only if maintainers explicitly document and test that Claw-owned cron jobs intentionally survive agent deletion and have a supported recovery owner.

options.title: Defer cron lifecycle
options.body: Remove this cron slice from the stack until the shared agent-deletion ownership contract is settled.

recommendation.title: Adopt canonical agent cleanup
recommendation.body: Update the shared agent-deletion path to remove and reconcile agent-owned cron jobs, with Claw removal layering only Claw-specific provenance cleanup around it.
